pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A melodic percussion instrument is one that (1 mark)
   A. is always loud
   B. can play different notes to make a tune
   C. has no parts
   D. can only make one sound

2. Why must the tin of charcoal stay closed until it is cold? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   B. The charcoal will become white
   C. The charcoal will taste bad
   D. The tin will float

3. On a xylophone, the long bars give (1 mark)
   A. low notes
   B. only clapping sounds
   C. high notes
   D. no sound

4. What does pivoting mean? (1 mark)
   A. Running quickly
   B. Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   C. Jumping over the ball
   D. Dropping the ball

5. The game restarts after each goal with (1 mark)
   A. a centre pass
   B. a jump ball
   C. a throw-in from the side
   D. a penalty kick

6. A player who catches the ball must not (1 mark)
   A. pass it
   B. run with it
   C. pivot on the landing foot
   D. throw it to a teammate

7. In a chest pass your thumbs turn downwards (1 mark)
   A. before you catch
   B. when you sit
   C. never
   D. as you release the ball

8. On the colour wheel, green sits between (1 mark)
   A. orange and purple
   B. red and yellow
   C. yellow and blue
   D. red and blue

9. The French rhythm name for a pair of quavers is (1 mark)
   A. tee-taa
   B. taa
   C. rest
   D. ta-te

10. How many beats does each bar have in the four-beat patterns of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Two
   C. Eight
   D. Four

11. Which pattern has three beats of sound and one beat of silence? (1 mark)
   A. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   B. taa taa taa taa
   C. taa taa taa (rest)
   D. (rest) (rest) (rest) (rest)

12. How long does one quaver last? (1 mark)
   A. One beat
   B. A quarter of a beat only
   C. Half a beat
   D. Two beats

13. What makes ending on d good for a short melody? (1 mark)
   A. It sounds unfinished
   B. It is the highest note
   C. It sounds finished and at rest
   D. It is the loudest note

14. On the Kenyan flag, black stands for (1 mark)
   A. the people of Kenya
   B. the land
   C. the sea
   D. peace

15. Where should you stay during a sprint race? (1 mark)
   A. Across all lanes
   B. In your own lane
   C. On the grass beside the track
   D. In any lane

16. Where should your hands be at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Just behind the start line
   B. Far in front of the line
   C. In your pockets
   D. Over the line

17. The Kenyan flag has stripes of (1 mark)
   A. orange and green
   B. black, red and green with thin white stripes
   C. blue, yellow and white
   D. red, white and blue

18. On the Kenyan flag, white stands for (1 mark)
   A. peace and honesty
   B. blood
   C. the people
   D. the sky

19. In a side roll, your body should be (1 mark)
   A. curled like a ball
   B. straight and long like a log
   C. bent at the waist
   D. hanging in the air

20. For a well-lit photograph of a person, the sun should be (1 mark)
   A. behind the person
   B. behind the photographer
   C. under the ground
   D. inside the lens

21. The centre of interest is (1 mark)
   A. the edge of the photo
   B. the camera button
   C. the main thing you want people to notice
   D. the middle of the room

22. If the bright sun is behind your subject, the subject will (1 mark)
   A. disappear
   B. be dark with the face in shadow
   C. be lit clearly
   D. turn blue

23. Which is a digital device for photography? (1 mark)
   A. Recorder
   B. Smartphone
   C. Ruler
   D. Kayamba

24. What is the danger of pointing a camera directly at the sun? (1 mark)
   A. It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture
   B. It saves the battery
   C. It makes the sun cooler
   D. It makes the picture sharper

25. Which joint has the mouthpiece? (1 mark)
   A. Middle joint
   B. Head joint
   C. None
   D. Foot joint

26. How many joints does a descant recorder have? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Three
   C. Two
   D. Six

27. How many finger holes are on the front of the descant recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Twelve
   C. Five
   D. Seven

28. For a good tone you should blow (1 mark)
   A. with your cheeks puffed for ever
   B. as hard as you can
   C. gently and steadily
   D. only in short puffs

29. Supine means (1 mark)
   A. face down
   B. curled
   C. face up
   D. standing

30. The hare hop is done (1 mark)
   A. by sitting
   B. by rolling
   C. by crawling
   D. by hopping forward with both feet like a hare

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how to make a slab and a coil from clay. (3 marks)

32. Describe the fingering for B, A and G. (3 marks)

33. What does it mean to appreciate a work of Creative Arts? (2 marks)

34. Explain where the sun should be when you photograph a person and why. (3 marks)

35. Why is it important to warm up before doing gymnastics? (3 marks)

36. Explain why only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack can score goals. (3 marks)

37. Give four steps of a double-handed catch. (4 marks)

38. Describe how you would enter the pool and perform a glide safely. (5 marks)

39. What is a sequence in gymnastics? Give an example. (3 marks)

40. Describe the roles in a folk song performance. (4 marks)

41. State three ways of showing fair play in a netball game. (3 marks)

42. What is the East African Community? (3 marks)

43. Describe the procedure of making charcoal sticks for drawing, from cutting to cooling. (5 marks)

44. What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each. (3 marks)

45. Explain the job of the drumhead and the shell of a drum. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — can play different notes to make a tune
   Melodic instruments such as the xylophone play notes of different pitch.

2. A — Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   Air can make hot charcoal burn, so we wait until it is fully cool.

3. A — low notes
   Longer bars vibrate more slowly and sound lower.

4. B — Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   A player keeps one foot down and turns on it.

5. A — a centre pass
   The game restarts with a centre pass, and the teams take turns.

6. B — run with it
   Running with the ball is against the rules.

7. D — as you release the ball
   Thumbs turn down as the arms straighten and the ball leaves the hands.

8. C — yellow and blue
   Green sits between the two primary colours that make it.

9. D — ta-te
   Ta-te is two short sounds in one beat.

10. D — Four
   The patterns of this lesson have four beats.

11. C — taa taa taa (rest)
   Only the first has a single rest and three sounding beats.

12. C — Half a beat
   A quaver is half a beat.

13. C — It sounds finished and at rest
   Ending on the home note gives a complete feeling.

14. A — the people of Kenya
   Black represents the people of Kenya.

15. B — In your own lane
   Running in your lane prevents crashes.

16. A — Just behind the start line
   Hands go on the ground just behind the line.

17. B — black, red and green with thin white stripes
   The flag has black, red, green and white.

18. A — peace and honesty
   White stands for peace and honesty.

19. B — straight and long like a log
   A straight, tight body rolls smoothly.

20. B — behind the photographer
   Light falls on the front of the subject.

21. C — the main thing you want people to notice
   It draws the eye first.

22. B — be dark with the face in shadow
   The face is in shadow.

23. B — Smartphone
   A smartphone has a camera lens and digital memory.

24. A — It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture
   Looking at the sun harms the eyes.

25. B — Head joint
   The mouthpiece is at the top of the head joint.

26. B — Three
   Head joint, middle joint and foot joint.

27. D — Seven
   There are seven on the front and one thumb hole at the back.

28. C — gently and steadily
   A gentle, steady breath gives a warm tone.

29. C — face up
   Supine is lying on the back.

30. D — by hopping forward with both feet like a hare
   Small quick hops.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Flatten the clay with a rolling pin until even for a slab. Roll a small piece between palms for a coil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the slab, 1 mark for the coil, 1 mark for even thickness.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each note.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: To notice, understand and value it, giving reasons for what you think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind the photographer, so light falls on the front of the person. If the sun is behind the subject, the face is in shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 2 marks for the reason.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Warm-up prepares the muscles and joints, prevents injury and helps you perform better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Netball rules say only these two attackers may shoot, and only from inside the goal circle. Other players help by passing the ball to them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two players, 1 mark for the goal circle, 1 mark for the role of the others.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Watch the ball into your hands; reach out with both hands; spread the fingers with the thumbs close; bend the arms and pull the ball to the chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Get permission and warm up. Enter feet first by the steps or sit and slide. Stay in shallow water. Stand with the back to the wall and stretch the arms overhead. Put feet on the wall, breathe, put the face in, push off gently and glide with a straight body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five parts.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: A set of movements done in a fixed order. For example crab balance, lower to the mat, lie straight, side roll.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the correct example.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads the song; the chorus answers or repeats; the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat; dancers move to the music.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Follow the rules; respect the umpire; shake hands with the other team; take turns in positions; encourage teammates. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A group of countries in East Africa that work together on matters such as trade, travel and peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of countries, 1 mark for East Africa, 1 mark for working together.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Cut dry, straight twigs about the length of a hand. Trim off bark, knots and leaves. Pack the twigs tightly in a tin and close the lid with a small hole. An adult burns the tin in a fire until the smoke stops. Leave the tin closed to cool completely before opening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cutting, trimming, packing, burning by an adult, and cooling.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: The drumhead vibrates when struck and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drumhead, 2 marks for the shell's job explained.
